provenance: Official record: yes, reshaped by BetaNYC with some fields left out (values unchanged).

Read-only requests to the Checkbook NYC API (https://www.checkbooknyc.com/api, data domain Spending) at the moment you ask. No key is needed. The server sends at most one request per second, the limit the Comptroller's office set.

Reshaped by BetaNYC, some fields left out (values unchanged): The API answers in XML. The server turns each record into JSON with the API's own field names and every value unchanged, kept as text so codes keep their leading zeros. Each tool asks the API for a set list of fields, so fields the API offers but the tool does not ask for are left out.

dataset.scopeNote: Caveat: The Comptroller does not publish an update schedule for checkbooknyc.com. The README of the Checkbook NYC software says a typical frequency for loading data is a few times per week, but does not say how often the Comptroller's own site loads it. Caveat: Checkbook NYC links every page to the Comptroller's website disclaimer, which says the Comptroller does not guarantee that the information is accurate, complete or current, and that commercial use of the materials needs the Comptroller's written permission. Caveat: Figures depend on what City agencies report to the Comptroller's office. Records may be incomplete, delayed, or reflect later amendments, so check important figures on checkbooknyc.com. Caveat: A count of zero means the API found no matching records. When the API cannot be reached or refuses a request, the tool answers with an error instead.
